season_garden_entry.speaker: narrator
season_garden_entry.text: The orchard gate stood open on a morning when every nearby gate seemed to be resisting spring. Lin Yue stopped before the threshold and adjusted her bag against her uninjured side. Rain had washed pale strips down the old plaster wall. Through the opening she saw a branch lying across the path, its buds swollen and still green. Somebody had tied red cloth to each end so walkers would see it before their feet found the wood.

season_garden_01_002.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_002.text: The season of public trials had ended. Its three afternoons and the facility's twenty-four-copper allocation belonged to that completed arrangement, with their actual use and return recorded there. This invitation came from another place and offered different work. Yue had read it at home beside her own calendar. She had crossed out unavailable hours before bringing the page, including any home interval or accepted work her current records required.

season_garden_01_003.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_003.text: Qiu Lian was standing behind the gate, examining the broken branch. She wore the same practical cinnabar robe Yue recognized, its charcoal cuffs newly mended with darker thread. Recognition did not decide how closely they would work. Whatever they had actually chosen at the trial remained theirs; neither a shared acquaintance nor an invitation made friendship compulsory. Qiu lifted her gaze when Yue stopped. The first thing she said was that the branch had fallen after the rain.

season_garden_01_004.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_01_004.text: “That doesn't tell me whether it was sound before the rain,” Qiu added. “Or whether somebody climbed it. The gardener has closed this path until the damaged trees are inspected. I can see three places where people have already stepped over the cloth.” She tapped one boot against a dry patch. “A shortcut is very persuasive when the proper path goes around the entire building. I was about to take it myself. Then I saw the split above my head.”

season_garden_01_005.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_01_005.text: “I was looking at the ground,” Yue said. She stepped back far enough to see the hanging split. At the trial, a rival had been easy to imagine as somebody watching the same dial. Here the things they noticed were already different. Qiu's warning spared Yue a risky step without changing the relation between them into a debt. Yue thanked her plainly. Beyond the wall, a wooden shovel scraped twice and stopped. Somebody called that visitors should use the side entrance.

season_garden_01_006.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_006.text: The side entrance led through the dining hall, where mismatched bowls dried upside down on a shelf. An older woman was cutting spring greens with a knife so small it seemed unequal to her pile. She pointed with the handle toward two stools. Yue chose the one with a back. Qiu remained standing until the woman asked whether the floor was more comfortable. That earned a quick smile and then, reluctantly, a seated Qiu. Their bags rested beneath separate stools.

season_garden_01_007.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_007.text: Su Yao arrived carrying a plain cloth bundle. Her trial tablet was absent. In its place she had brought a folded garden schedule and an ordinary key lent for this meeting. She was helping the orchard households settle a repair arrangement for this finite season; she had not acquired clinical authority by changing buildings. The distinction appeared in the way she waited for Ren Qiao before discussing any room used by patients. Until he came, they spoke only about the kitchen doorway.

season_garden_01_008.speaker: rival_su_yao
season_garden_01_008.text: “There is no prize here,” Su said. “There are twenty three-hour maintenance sessions across ten weeks, on the two afternoons already offered. Each of you may accept only the sessions your real calendar leaves free. A missed session is unpaid; a changed date needs agreement before anyone expects attendance. We need light work on furniture, planting beds and shelter fittings. Heavy lifting, damaged trees and treatment belong to qualified staff. You can decline this invitation before we make the first appointment.”

season_garden_01_009.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_009.text: Yue heard the words without hurrying to answer. Twenty afternoons had the inviting shape of a finished thing. She knew how easily she could mistake a neat shape for available strength. The pain in her shoulder was ordinary that morning, dull and contained, but the stool's back was doing useful work. She laid her current calendar between the bowls and marked a rest interval after every proposed visit. Qiu watched the marks, then opened her own page instead of leaning over Yue's.

season_garden_01_010.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_01_010.text: “I can make the offered afternoons if my sister's visit stays where we have placed it,” Qiu said. “The visit will not become a repair session because somebody needs one more pair of hands. If those dates change, I'll tell you before accepting a replacement.” She held the page flat with two fingers. Her voice was brisk; the promise underneath it was less easy. Yue noticed an entire morning left empty between two crowded columns, and did not ask what the emptiness protected.

season_garden_01_011.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_011.text: Ren Qiao came from the healing hall with his medicine satchel fastened and a damp cuff folded back. He looked older in plain daylight than Yue remembered from the orchard's earlier rooms. The resemblance belonged to an existing person, not an assurance that every earlier encounter had happened in this journey. He introduced his responsibilities again for this arrangement. Patient assessment, treatment and changes to recovery plans remained with the licensed clinical team. Garden helpers could make an agreed space easier to use.

season_garden_01_012.speaker: ren_qiao
season_garden_01_012.text: “A comfortable seat can help somebody remain for the rest their treatment needs,” Ren said. “It does not diagnose the reason they are tired. A handrail can make a route manageable. It does not promise the strength to walk it. If somebody asks you to tell them whether their pain is dangerous, find us. If they ask you to move a cup, ask where they want it.” He smiled faintly. “Most care begins with a question small enough to answer.”

season_garden_01_013.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_013.text: The cutting knife resumed its patient scrape. Yue liked that sound more than the word care, which people sometimes made so large that it swallowed the person needing it. Qiu had turned her page toward Ren. She asked which rooms remained open while the damage was inspected. He drew the permitted route with his finger: dining hall, healing hall by its wide door, and the small court beside the intact plum. The fallen tree's former shelter and the upper path stayed closed.

season_garden_01_014.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_014.text: Their wages would come from a new garden repair reserve of one hundred sixty copper, supplied by the households using the orchard and held by its own treasurer. One hundred twenty covered two helpers at three copper for each completed three-hour session; forty covered agreed materials. The trial's old facility grant supplied none of it. Su placed the reserve's actual tally beside the terms. Any reduced attendance would leave the corresponding labor money unspent, rather than divide it into an unearned bonus.

season_garden_01_015.speaker: rival_su_yao
season_garden_01_015.text: “We pay completed time for the agreed light work,” Su said. “We do not pay you for a cure, a yield, a quick return to work or a person saying they feel better. Those things have different causes and owners. If a rain closure stops a session before it begins, we agree another available date or cancel it. If staff stop work for safety after it begins, the time actually worked is paid at the stated rate, with no penalty for obeying.”

season_garden_01_016.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_01_016.text: “And if I have to stop because of my shoulder?” Yue asked. The question seemed to place the ache in the middle of the table, among all the clean bowls. She resisted an impulse to promise that she would avoid causing trouble. Su asked what would make the arrangement usable. Yue said she needed ordinary freedom to pause, change an assigned light task with agreement, or end a session. A paid hour already completed should remain completed. Future hours should remain future hours.

season_garden_01_017.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_017.text: They agreed that partial completed time would be reckoned at one copper per hour, with no need to finish an unsafe motion to earn it. There would be no fee for leaving the arrangement, and no claim on either practitioner's own method book. Their cultivation remained Qi Gathering, fifth stage, Four pairs. Neither a maintenance wage nor a useful plant would grant another pair, enlarge their tested capacity or make either woman a healer. Qiu said the terms were almost disappointingly ordinary.

season_garden_01_018.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_01_018.text: “I mean that as praise,” Qiu added when Su raised an eyebrow. “I know how to close a small load quickly. Here we are discussing hinges and shade. If I demonstrate a method, it will be on the appropriate external practice fixture under its own permission, within my tested limits. Nobody is going to put a patient's rest under that fixture and call the result a treatment.” She folded her calendar. “I can still be impatient about a hinge. You will discover that.”

season_garden_01_019.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_019.text: The woman with the greens laughed aloud. She had listened while continuing to work, with the particular confidence of somebody whose breakfast could not wait for a philosophy to finish. She asked if they had settled enough terms to eat. The kitchen's food was available at its posted ordinary meal price; it was neither a wage deduction nor a hidden promise of limitless board. Yue paid from her own purse and chose the smaller bowl. Hunger had already begun making every sentence feel sharper.

season_garden_01_020.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_020.text: As they ate, the older woman described the storm through kitchen facts. A pot had cracked because the shelf beneath it shifted. They had moved supper twice and served the last bowls cold. The tree that fell had sheltered the doorway for forty-three springs, if the oldest neighbor's count was right. Nobody had been under it when it broke. Even that fortunate fact left the kitchen without shade, the path without shelter and a familiar place altered beyond the damage to its wood.

season_garden_01_021.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_021.text: Yue looked through the open door. The fallen tree's stump was hidden from this permitted angle, but an unfamiliar slice of sky appeared where its crown had been. Grief did not always announce itself as a death in a bed. Sometimes it was the brightness at a doorway where people had rested through decades of summers. She could not restore those summers with an accurate measurement. She could, however, listen while the woman remembered which branch had held the festival lantern.

season_garden_01_022.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_01_022.text: “We should put the shelter back before the first hot week,” Qiu said. “People cannot sit comfortably under a memory.” The woman stopped cutting. Her silence changed the shape of the table. Qiu glanced at the knife and then at Yue. “That sounded cruel,” she said. “I meant the heat will not wait.” Nobody told her that good intentions had removed the sentence. After a moment, the woman said both things were true: the missing tree and the approaching heat.

season_garden_01_023.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_023.text: Qiu apologized without making the table comfort her. She asked which seat the woman missed most. The answer was the bench with one short leg, because that was where her husband had waited during his last well summer. The bench itself had survived. It stood in storage now, dirty and uneven, and she did not want it burned with the fallen branches. Yue felt the sudden temptation to promise its rescue before anyone had inspected its joints. She swallowed that promise with her last mouthful.

season_garden_01_024.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_024.text: They went first to the storage edge adjoining the dining hall. Staff brought the old bench onto a low work area; neither Yue nor Qiu lifted its weight. Their assignment was to examine accessible surfaces, measure the wobble while it was unloaded, and report what a qualified furniture worker should check before use. Qiu produced her small bronze gauge. Yue laid a folded cloth beneath the damaged corner. The cloth steadied their observation without converting the bench into something safe to sit on.

season_garden_01_025.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_025.text: The underside smelled of dry dust and sour old oil. One leg had a wedge driven into it, carefully enough that Yue could imagine the hands doing the work. A scratched line ran beneath the seat, followed by a name neither helper tried to read into an entire history. Qiu measured the unequal feet and marked the figures on their assigned repair sheet. Yue traced the edge of a loose peg without pulling it. A carpenter would decide whether it belonged there.

season_garden_01_026.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_01_026.text: “If we replace every crooked part, will it still be the bench she asked for?” Yue said. She was not asking Qiu to decide the owner's attachment. The question concerned the estimate they would bring back: repair, replacement or no safe public use. Qiu sat on her heels and looked along the grain. “If it collapses under her, I doubt resemblance will console anyone.” Yue agreed. Their disagreement remained inside the harder question of what safe repair could honestly preserve.

season_garden_01_027.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_027.text: A staff carpenter inspected the joints and pointed out a split neither woman's first view had shown. The bench could be repaired with a new side rail and a properly fitted foot, preserving the seat and most sound timber. Until that work and a load check were complete, it would remain out of use. The cost was six copper from the separate materials allowance, subject to the owner agreeing that repair. Qiu wrote the estimate clearly enough that it could survive being read by somebody else.

season_garden_01_028.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_028.text: The kitchen woman came to look before the carpenter began. Her finger rested on the worn seat, exactly where a seated palm had polished it over years. She approved the necessary replacement pieces and asked to retain the old rail afterward. The carpenter explained that it would not serve as a support. She said she knew; she wanted a piece for her shelf. Yue saw no contradiction in keeping a useless piece of wood when nobody expected it to carry a person.

season_garden_01_029.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_029.text: At the healing hall's doorway, an older patient watched the exchange from a chair provided by staff. She asked when the repaired bench would be ready. Ren Qiao answered that the carpenter had a time estimate for the furniture, while her own walking plan would be discussed after the day's assessment. The patient made a displeased sound. She wanted an afternoon outside and was tired of every answer having a different clock. Yue recognized that anger before she could name anything helpful to say.

season_garden_01_030.speaker: ren_qiao
season_garden_01_030.text: “You can be tired of the clocks,” Ren said. “We still need to keep their claims separate.” He moved his chair closer, leaving her an easy line of sight. “A safe bench could be ready and your strength still not ready for the farther path. Or you could be ready for a short supported walk before this bench is repaired. We can look for an available seat along the route your present plan allows.” He waited while she considered the offered smaller afternoon.

season_garden_01_031.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_031.text: The patient accepted a visit to the intact tree's court, accompanied by the staff member already assigned to her. Yue and Qiu were not given clinical escort duties. They moved a light empty tray from the route after asking its owner, then let the pair pass without treating the walk as a demonstration of their own usefulness. The older woman's hand tightened on her support. She looked at the sky with an expression Yue could not reduce to either relief or disappointment.

season_garden_01_032.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_032.text: Qiu watched until they reached the court. “That took longer to arrange than the walk will take,” she said quietly. Yue answered that some arrangements made the walk possible. Qiu nodded, although agreement did not remove her impatience. She said her quick method existed because people could be harmed while a slow procedure was still being explained. Yue said a quick procedure could also leave harm beyond the moment its dial became quiet. Each had seen something worth protecting, and neither had disproved the other.

season_garden_01_033.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_033.text: A gust pushed through the wide doorway and rattled a loose shutter. It struck the sill hard enough to interrupt them. Yue stepped away while Qiu caught the empty light latch by its safe end, following the staff instruction given at the tour. The heavier panel was secured by its own ordinary restraint; she did not hold its weight with qi. They called the maintenance worker before examining the hinge. Wind was offering a practical subject before their disagreement could become too pleased with itself.

season_garden_01_034.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_034.text: The worker showed them a missing washer and a groove worn by years of hurried closing. A quick movement made the latch catch; it also drove the edge into the same damage each time. A slower guided movement avoided that groove but depended on somebody remembering the trick. The proper repair required the washer and a sound bearing surface. Until then, the staff would keep the shutter secured. Qiu looked almost offended by a hinge that refused to honor either woman's preferred timing.

season_garden_01_035.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_01_035.text: “I can close it fast or close it gently,” she said, “and both would be pretending the missing part had somehow become my skill.” She wrote the needed washer on the materials request. Yue smiled, then stopped before the smile became a victory. The worker had identified the fault. Their contribution was the observation and a clear report. The worker's trained judgment had supplied the missing explanation. Qiu caught the change in her face. “You may enjoy it a little,” she said.

season_garden_01_036.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_036.text: They were assigned a small planting bed near the court after the gardener had checked that approach. Its timber edging had shifted in the rain, letting soil spill into the accessible route. Heavy resetting belonged to the gardener and another worker. Yue and Qiu could remove light loose debris with hand tools, sort usable seed markers and prepare a clear inventory of what had washed away. The bed would not be rebuilt to an attractive shape before its drainage was examined.

season_garden_01_037.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_037.text: The first marker Yue lifted carried a fading label for a medicinal root. She did not treat the name as instructions for its use. Its harvest belonged to the apothecary's known stock and clinical processes; an unidentified surviving plant would be checked by the responsible gardener and dispenser. She placed uncertain markers in a separate shallow box. Qiu asked whether she wanted every faded thing separated. Yue answered that she wanted uncertainty visible before somebody used a guess to fill a jar.

season_garden_01_038.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_038.text: Qiu made a second box for readable markers, then discovered that readable words could still belong to displaced plants. The two boxes multiplied into three without any new philosophy being required. The older kitchen woman brought an empty crock for the doubtful pieces and asked why they had not used that first. Yue admitted they had begun with the containers easiest to reach. It was a mild embarrassment, improved by the fact that the crock fit the shelf much better than their elegant arrangement.

season_garden_01_039.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_039.text: Their tools were ordinary short-handled scoops. Yue used her uninjured side and changed position whenever the movement began tugging at her shoulder. Qiu first matched her pace, then caught herself and asked whether that was useful company or an irritating kind of supervision. Yue said she preferred separate work with a clear shared stopping signal for the route. Qiu moved to the other end. The space between them let each woman notice her own tiredness instead of guessing it from the other's hands.

season_garden_01_040.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_040.text: A young visitor entered the court carrying a paper pinwheel. His patched sleeve was rolled above one wrist, and he kept asking his accompanying adult whether the paper might catch the breeze. He asked whether the women were planting a tree that would grow by tomorrow. Qiu said tomorrow was much too soon. He considered that an unhelpful design. Yue asked what he wanted the tree to do tomorrow. He wanted to hang the pinwheel where his grandmother could see it from her chair.

season_garden_01_041.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_01_041.text: “We can ask whether there is a safe place for the pinwheel today,” Yue said. “A tree would need its own growing time.” The child brightened at the smaller possibility. Staff approved a low hook already outside the walking line, and his grandmother agreed to the arrangement. Qiu held the string while he tied it himself. The pinwheel turned in the passing wind. It was not a substitute for the fallen crown, but it answered the question the child had actually brought.

season_garden_01_042.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_042.text: The grandmother laughed when she saw it, then began to cry. The child looked alarmed and reached for the string. She stopped him gently. The tears were hers and did not mean he had done harm. Yue stood far enough away to let their conversation remain private. Qiu lowered the unused string into the child's bag. Neither practitioner tried to make the crying end so that the successful small task could remain uncomplicated. A moving scrap of paper could arrive inside grief without curing it.

season_garden_01_043.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_043.text: At the agreed rest break, Yue sat beside the intact plum rather than beneath a damaged limb. Her shoulder's ache had sharpened into a line she knew better than to ignore. She described the change to the responsible staff member and stopped the tool work pending the ordinary advice she was given. Nobody asked Qiu to evaluate the injury. Ren Qiao later checked Yue within his clinical role and advised the day's specific limits. Work planning followed that assessment instead of replacing it.

season_garden_01_044.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_044.text: Qiu kept her own break. She rolled her cord and unrolled it, an unnecessary motion that gave her hands something to do while the bed remained visibly unfinished. Yue asked if she disliked resting or disliked being seen at rest. Qiu said the distinction sounded like a trap, but answered it anyway. Being unseen at work had taught her to make visible work whenever someone might be looking. She could stop for a clock. Stopping because her own body mattered felt less exact.

season_garden_01_045.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_045.text: Yue had no prepared cure for that habit. She offered half her orange after asking whether Qiu wanted it. Qiu accepted and spent a surprisingly long time removing every pale thread. Their silence carried no required intimacy. A rival, a possible collaborator or a person met at a respectful distance could share fruit on the same permitted bench. Across the court, the pinwheel faltered as the wind dropped. Nothing terrible followed the stopping. Yue noticed Qiu watching it and chose not to turn the image into advice.

season_garden_01_046.speaker: rival_su_yao
season_garden_01_046.text: Su brought the first session's work sheet at the end of the break. “Tell me what remains open,” she said. Qiu listed the bed's drainage, the shutter repair and the bench's qualified repair. Yue listed the uncertain plant labels and her own changed work limit. Su wrote none of these as failures. They were live conditions for future work. The sheet would travel to the appropriate owners, while personal clinical details stayed with the clinic. The garden needed the agreed work limit, not Yue's private examination.

season_garden_01_047.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_047.text: The remaining hour could include light sorting at a table, if Yue accepted that task and its permitted movements. She agreed after checking the instruction against how her shoulder felt. Qiu asked to work at the neighboring table on the readable markers, leaving the doubtful plants to the gardener. Their difference in speed became easy to see. Qiu finished her first tray before Yue had finished half of hers. She set down the second tray with care, resisting the invitation to race somebody else's limit.

season_garden_01_048.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_048.text: A marker snapped under Yue's fingers. Its timber had softened along a hidden crack. She startled, feeling an irrational shame at damaging something already damaged. Qiu fetched the small waste container without announcing the event. Then she asked whether the remaining pieces should stay together for identification. Yue nodded. The gardener later said the plant had a second sound marker and needed no reconstruction from the broken one. A lost label had briefly made Yue feel as if she had lost the whole bed.

season_garden_01_049.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_01_049.text: “I wanted this afternoon to prove I could do useful work without paying for it tomorrow,” Yue said. She had kept the words until Qiu was close enough to hear them privately. “A broken stick shouldn't decide that.” Qiu said she had wanted the afternoon to prove that speed could be kind. They looked toward the repaired shutter's locked position. Neither proof would be completed in one visit. Their hands had done actual useful tasks while the larger questions remained inconveniently alive.

season_garden_01_050.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_050.text: The gardener brought two possible priorities for the next session. The accessible route needed a low border that would stop loose soil reaching it; the shelter seating needed light fittings prepared before the carpenter returned. Heavy construction belonged to staff in either case. Both requests were real and neither could fill their one next afternoon. Yue felt the familiar pull toward selecting the task with the clearest visible finish. Then she remembered the patient's hand gripping her support along the route.

season_garden_01_051.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_051.text: Qiu preferred preparing the seating fittings because they could be completed within a session and immediately reduce the carpenter's later delay. Yue preferred beginning the route border because people were already walking around a spill. Their arguments stayed attached to those users and schedules. The gardener explained the temporary route protections and the carpenter's confirmed date before letting either preference harden into a moral claim. With that information, the choice could describe a tradeoff somebody would actually live with.

season_garden_01_052.speaker: rival_su_yao
season_garden_01_052.text: “You will choose the first shared maintenance priority,” Su said. “The other request remains open with its owner; choosing one does not make it disappear. We will review both after the fourth visit, using what the staff and users have actually observed. Do not promise that your first preference is an identity you must defend for ten weeks.” She looked between them. “And do not promise the unchosen work at night. A schedule drawn around real rest needs to survive enthusiasm.”

season_garden_01_053.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_053.text: Before making that choice, Yue walked to the kitchen doorway and thanked the older woman for telling them about the bench. She did not describe the woman's memory on the work sheet. The owner had authorized a repair and retained the old rail; the memory could remain a story spoken at a table. The woman offered to show them the place where her husband had carved a small bird. Yue said she would like to see it once the safe inspection was finished.

season_garden_01_054.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_054.text: The carpenter had already separated the worn rail. Its underside held the bird, clumsy and unmistakable once the woman pointed. Qiu studied the carving with an expression that had lost its usual quick readiness. The woman said her husband had made it during a summer when he could no longer walk far, and had been annoyed that the wings resembled leaves. She laughed through the memory. Yue found herself seeing a whole afternoon that the account books would never need to contain.

season_garden_01_055.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_055.text: At the session's close, Su recorded the three hours actually completed within the amended assignments. Each helper received three copper from the garden's labor reserve, separately acknowledged. The bench's authorized six-copper material cost would be paid to the carpenter on its agreed completion; no money had yet been handed to the helpers for that repair. Yue placed her wage in her purse without calling it a reward for endurance. The useful choice to stop had been part of a completed working afternoon.

season_garden_01_056.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_01_056.text: “I thought you would apologize when you changed the task,” Qiu said as they gathered their tools. Yue answered that she had thought so too. Qiu tightened the cord around her small gauge. “I am glad you didn't. I dislike hearing an apology when what somebody means is that a joint hurts.” Her bluntness made Yue smile. It did not make the shoulder stop hurting. The smile and the ache could occupy the same moment without either serving as a verdict.

season_garden_01_057.speaker: narrator
season_garden_01_057.text: Outside the dining hall, the two women checked the next offered afternoon against their calendars one last time. The agreed visit fitted both, with the rest and existing obligations already protected. The trial's clocks were long gone; this garden had its own ten-week boundary and twenty ordinary sessions. A bird called from the intact plum. The fallen tree remained fallen beyond the closed route. Yue was ready to choose their first priority because the decision concerned a next task, not the worth of either life.

season_garden_priority_choice.speaker: narrator
season_garden_priority_choice.text: The gardener laid two small drawings on the table. One showed a low border beside the accessible route, prepared in light sections for staff to fit; the other showed the shelter's seating fittings, prepared ahead of the carpenter's confirmed return. The temporary route protections could remain while seating came first, and the existing indoor seats could remain while the route came first. Neither option removed the other request. Yue would choose the work their next available session began, with a review after the fourth visit.

choices.text: Prepare the accessible route border first.
Prepare the shelter seating fittings first.

season_garden_priority_route_01.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_priority_route_01.text: “I want to begin with the route,” Yue said. “People are using it every day, and the spill makes the turn awkward even with the temporary boards. The border will not cure anybody's weakness. It can remove a small extra problem from a journey that is already difficult.” She set her hand beside the drawing. She had made a preference aloud without describing the seating request as vain. The bench owner still needed an answer about a place to sit.

season_garden_priority_route_02.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_priority_route_02.text: Qiu accepted the selection, then asked that they prepare the seating fittings on the next available session rather than leave them under the broad word later. The carpenter's scheduled return could still be met if the tasks remained distinct. “I will help with the border,” she said. “I also want us to remember what we postponed. If the border work grows, we ask its owner before allowing it to eat the bench.” Her caution was useful precisely because she had preferred the other drawing.

season_garden_priority_route_03.speaker: narrator
season_garden_priority_route_03.text: Su noted the selected first priority and retained the seating request with its actual date. The route's temporary protection would stay until the gardener installed and checked the prepared sections. Yue and Qiu were accepting preparation of light pieces, not final structural approval. The carpenter confirmed that the seating fittings could be ready after their following available session. The owner had not lost her repair because Yue chose another afternoon first. She had gained a clear date instead of a vague promise.

season_garden_priority_route_04.speaker: narrator
season_garden_priority_route_04.text: The patient who had taken the supported walk heard the plan from the staff member responsible for the route. She wanted to know whether the new border would make the farther path open. The answer was no: damaged trees and the closed upper shelter required their own inspections and repairs. She frowned, then asked whether the short permitted turn would be easier. That was the exact purpose being checked. Yue stood nearby without adding a larger hope to soften the smaller truthful answer.

season_garden_priority_route_05.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_priority_route_05.text: “I keep wanting to say something better after a small answer,” Yue told Qiu when the patient had gone inside. “As if a useful improvement needs a grander promise to be worth making.” Qiu ran her thumb along the drawing's edge. “I keep wanting the small answer to arrive faster,” she said. Their old disagreement had found another ordinary place to live. Here speed meant the time until an actual clear route existed, not the speed of a practiced hand at a demonstration table.

season_garden_priority_route_06.speaker: narrator
season_garden_priority_route_06.text: They counted the light border pieces needed and left the cutting of sound timber to the gardener's maintenance worker. Preparation would use existing safe offcuts, with the responsible worker inspecting their suitability; extra material would require a price and approval from the forty-copper allowance. Yue did not carry a bundle home. Qiu did not promise to shape it at night. Their next session was already chosen, and the rest of their evening still belonged to their own lives.

season_garden_priority_route_07.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_priority_route_07.text: At the gate Qiu stopped beside the red cloth and looked again at the hanging split. “The border is not the dangerous tree,” she said. “But it is a thing we can finish under the real limit of this job. I would like that to remain a reason for doing it, even if nobody notices our names.” Yue answered that she would notice the difference when she walked through. Qiu said she hoped the people who needed it would notice something easier than their work.

season_garden_priority_route_08.speaker: narrator
season_garden_priority_route_08.text: Yue left through the side entrance with the route drawing's permitted copy folded in her bag. The seating date remained on the shared work sheet, and the review after the fourth visit would ask what both requests had become. Her wage made a small ordinary weight against her purse. She took the shorter walk home because her shoulder had already asked enough of the day. Choosing a route priority at the orchard did not require her to make every route in her own life longer.

season_garden_priority_seats_01.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_priority_seats_01.text: “Let's prepare the seating fittings first,” Yue said. “The carpenter has a confirmed return, and if we miss it the usable outdoor seat may wait much longer. The route has its temporary protection for now. I want its border kept as the next specific task, with staff checking that temporary turn each day.” She touched the carpenter's date rather than the clean shape of the drawing. The choice concerned a chance to finish safe work on time, not making the shelter pretty for visitors.

season_garden_priority_seats_02.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_priority_seats_02.text: Qiu's pleased expression appeared and vanished before it could become a victory over Yue. “Then I owe the route concern proper attention,” she said. “If the temporary boards make somebody's turn unmanageable before our next session, staff must tell us. We can change the order by agreement.” She marked the next route session while Su watched. Being chosen first did not make the seating task immune to facts arriving later. Yue found that answer more reassuring than Qiu promising to be right.

season_garden_priority_seats_03.speaker: narrator
season_garden_priority_seats_03.text: Su recorded the seating preparation and the gardener retained responsibility for the temporary route protections. The carpenter confirmed the light fittings the helpers could safely prepare and the exact pieces staff would install. Yue and Qiu would not approve the repaired bench for use. Their work could shorten the carpenter's later preparation while his inspection and load check remained his own. The bench owner listened to the plan without being asked to become grateful before a sound seat actually existed.

season_garden_priority_seats_04.speaker: narrator
season_garden_priority_seats_04.text: The older woman brought the retained rail wrapped in a towel and showed them the carved bird once more. She asked whether the new rail could have a bird too. Qiu began to say yes, then looked at the carpenter. He said decoration on a suitable nonstructural surface could be discussed after the repair, with no cut weakening its support. The woman preferred a painted bird on the end. A remembered detail had found a safe future form without dictating every part of the furniture.

season_garden_priority_seats_05.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_priority_seats_05.text: “I don't know how to paint a bird,” Yue admitted. The woman said that her husband's bird had looked like leaves and survived forty summers anyway. Qiu suggested a removable small painted plaque after the bench was approved, if the owner wanted it and a painter could spare the time. That was an offered possibility, not unpaid work assigned to an absent person. Yue laughed at the sudden freedom of allowing beauty to wait for somebody who actually knew how to make it.

season_garden_priority_seats_06.speaker: narrator
season_garden_priority_seats_06.text: They laid out the light fittings on a table and counted only the pieces the carpenter had named. Existing sound stock covered them, subject to his own suitability check. The six-copper authorized repair cost remained the present estimate; any change required the owner and treasurer's agreement before spending. Qiu returned the bronze gauge to its cord. Its careful numbers could help prepare the work, but neither precision nor speed permitted them to replace the carpenter's judgment with their own confidence.

season_garden_priority_seats_07.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_priority_seats_07.text: “This is the sort of waiting I find hardest,” Qiu said. “The pieces are here, and I can see where they go, but the safe completion belongs to somebody else's work.” Yue said waiting could still have a clear edge: a real appointment, a stated handover, a person responsible. Qiu considered that. “Then I will stop pretending I am being patient when I am merely losing track of the edge.” She checked the scheduled return once and put the date away.

season_garden_priority_seats_08.speaker: narrator
season_garden_priority_seats_08.text: Yue left with the seating preparation first on the agreed schedule and the route border still named for the next session. The review after the fourth visit would look at both, using actual use and staff observations rather than admiration for the decision. Her shoulder ached as she reached the ordinary street. She took the shorter way home and let the work remain at the orchard. A bench could wait for its carpenter without following her into the whole evening as an unfinished personal duty.
